texts.preamble: R. S. Treveni Foods Pvt. Ltd vs Authorized Officer on 9 February, 2016 Author: Sanjib Banerjee Bench: Sanjib Banerjee Od-5 Wp No.5 of 2016 In The High Court At Calcutta Constitutional Writ Jurisdiction Original Side R. S. Treveni Foods Pvt. Ltd. Versus Authorized Officer, Food Safety & Standard Authority Of India & Ors. Before: The Hon'ble Justice Sanjib Banerjee Date : 9th February, 2016. Appearance: Mr. Anubhav Sinha, Adv Mr. Arabinda Sen, Adv Mr. P. K. Roy, Ad Mr. K. K. Maiti, A Mr. Sudhir Kr. Mehta, Adv. The Court :
texts.facts: T dispute is as to whether an imported consignment of red lentil is fit for human consumption. The report from the laboratory where the last test was conducted revealed that the uric acid content in the goods is marginally higher at about 103.6 units agains the permissible 100 units. R. S. Treveni Foods Pvt. Ltd vs Authorized Officer on 9 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53544225/ 1 There is also a dispute between the parties as to whether a further appeal lies or whether the test can be conducted at some other place in an attempt to ascertain the veracity of the previous test. The respondent authorities have been gracious enough to concede, without this being treated as a precedent, that the goods may be tested at any other recognised laboratory. The respondent authorities have suggested that samples may be drawn in the presence of the petitioner's representatives and such samples be sealed in the presence of the petitioner's representatives before being forwarded to any recognised laboratory notified under Section 47 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The petitioner has indicated that the further tests may be conducted at the Export Inspection Agency Laboratory, Kolkata at 101, Southend Enclave, 1582, Rajdanga Main Road, Kolkata 700 107. All fresh samples would be sealed in such a manner that the petitioner or the respondent authorities would not be able to have access to the material without tampering the other's seal.
